lesson.text: Quick memory: last unit, phrases and clauses. What does every clause have? A subject and a verb, like "the dog barked".
A simple sentence has one independent clause: The wind blew.
A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with and, but, or or so: The wind blew, and the door banged.
A complex sentence has an independent clause and a dependent one: When the wind blew, the door banged.
A compound-complex sentence has two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause: When the wind blew, the door banged, and the dog barked.
Try it in the world: tell the story of your last adventure in the game in four sentences: one simple, one compound, one complex and one compound-complex. Next: misplaced modifiers.

exercises.prompt: Which is a simple sentence?
exercises.hint: Count the clauses: how many subject and verb pairs?
choices: The owl hooted, and the mice hid.
When the owl hooted, the mice hid.
exercises.explain: "The owl hooted." has one independent clause: a simple sentence.

exercises.prompt: Which is a compound sentence?
exercises.hint: Two independent clauses joined.
choices: I was hungry, so I ate.
Because I was hungry, I ate.
exercises.explain: Two independent clauses joined with "so".

exercises.prompt: A complex sentence has a dependent clause.
exercises.hint: Think of "When the wind blew, the door banged". What does "when" start?
exercises.explain: Yes: a complex sentence has a dependent clause and an independent one.

exercises.prompt: Which word could join two independent clauses?
exercises.hint: A joining word.
exercises.explain: "But" can join two independent clauses: I was tired, but I kept going.

exercises.prompt: Which is a complex sentence?
exercises.hint: Look for a part that starts with although, when or because.
exercises.explain: "Although it rained" is dependent.

exercises.prompt: What kind of sentence is "When the lights went out, we lit candles, and Gran told stories"?
exercises.hint: Two independent + one dependent.
exercises.explain: Two independent clauses and one dependent.

exercises.prompt: Turn "The rain stopped. We went out." into a complex sentence.
exercises.hint: Use when or after.
choices: When the rain stopped, we went out.
The rain stopped, we went out.
exercises.explain: "When the rain stopped" becomes dependent.

exercises.prompt: "She laughed, but he frowned" is a compound sentence.
exercises.hint: Two independent clauses with but.
exercises.explain: Yes: "She laughed" and "he frowned" are joined by but.

exercises.prompt: Why vary sentence kinds in writing?
exercises.hint: Think how it would read if every sentence were the same length.
choices: to make it interesting and clear
exercises.explain: Variety keeps writing lively and clear.

exercises.prompt: Which is NOT a complete sentence?
exercises.hint: Can it stand alone?
choices: The bus was late, so we walked.
exercises.explain: A dependent clause alone is a fragment.

exercises.prompt: Which is compound-complex?
exercises.hint: Count the clauses.
choices: If you finish, you can play, and I will cook.
If you finish, you can play.
exercises.explain: If you finish is a dependent clause; you can play and I will cook are two independent clauses joined by and. Two independent and one dependent: compound-complex.

exercises.prompt: What is the best way to join "The river rose" and "The road flooded" to show cause?
exercises.hint: Which choice tells you why the road flooded?
choices: Because the river rose, the road flooded.
The river rose, the road flooded.
The river rose and flooded road.
exercises.explain: Because the river rose is a dependent clause that gives the cause; the road flooded is the independent clause with the effect. Together they make a complex sentence.

exercises.prompt: How many independent clauses are in "We cheered, and the team waved"?
exercises.hint: Count those that stand alone.
exercises.explain: We cheered (subject we, verb cheered) and the team waved (subject the team, verb waved): 2 independent clauses, joined by and.

exercises.prompt: A compound-complex sentence needs at least one dependent clause.
exercises.hint: Split the name: compound, and complex. What does the complex part need?
exercises.explain: Yes: the complex part means at least one dependent clause.

exercises.prompt: Order from simplest to most complicated.
exercises.hint: Count the clauses.
exercises.explain: A simple sentence has one independent clause, a compound one has two, and a compound-complex one has two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences by kind.
items: I was hungry, so I ate.
When the bell rang, we left.
Because it was late, we slept.
exercises.hint: Count the clauses, then look for a joining word (and, but, so) or a starting word (when, because).
exercises.explain: The owl hooted and snow fell are simple. The so and but sentences are compound. The when and because sentences are complex.

exercises.prompt: Match each kind of sentence to what it has.
exercises.hint: Count the independent clauses first, then look for a dependent one.
exercises.explain: Simple: one independent clause. Compound: two independent. Complex: one independent and a dependent. Compound-complex: two independent and a dependent.

exercises.prompt: Sort the sentences: complex, or compound-complex?
items: When it rained, we hid, and the dog barked.
Because I was late, I ran.
If you finish, you can play, and I will cook.
Although she was tired, she sang.
exercises.hint: Count the independent clauses: one makes it complex, two (with a dependent clause) make it compound-complex.
exercises.explain: Complex: one independent clause and a dependent one (when it rained, because I was late, although she was tired). Compound-complex: two independent clauses and a dependent one.

exercises.prompt: How many clauses are in "When the wind blew, the door banged, and the dog barked"?
exercises.hint: Count each subject that has its own verb.
exercises.explain: The wind blew (dependent), the door banged and the dog barked (independent): 3 clauses, so it is a compound-complex sentence.

exercises.prompt: Build a compound-complex sentence: put the parts in order.
exercises.hint: Start with the dependent clause and its comma, then join two independent clauses with and.
exercises.explain: When the lights went out, Gran told a story, and we lit candles: one dependent clause, then two independent clauses joined by and.
